_doc: Container registry. The system fills these on a schedule — it never invents formats. Accent rule everywhere: <em> marks the minimum set of words that communicates the claim standalone; connectives stay white.

daily_recap.cadence: daily (one of the 5 daily slots, same time every day)
daily_recap.slides: cover (FIXED, identical every day) + 5-9 payload (one story each) + cta — 10-slide carousels measurably outperform short ones
daily_recap.cover_headline: WHAT JUST HAPPENED IN AI IN THE LAST 24 HOURS?
daily_recap.cover_rule: Cover NEVER changes except the photo collage (2-3 press images side by side). The repetition is the point — @technology runs this identical cover 4+ times a week; followers learn the habit.
daily_recap.payload_rule: One story per slide, strongest first: headline = the story's wild claim (JUST-formula, compressed), body = 2 sentences with bold facts. Media card when the press image passes. ALWAYS include one builder/inspiration item when any story qualifies (someone built something with AI/Claude Code and the viewer thinks 'wow, I want to do the same') — it gets the 'WHILE YOU SCROLLED, SOMEONE BUILT...' register.
daily_recap.why: The anchor habit format — followers return for it daily; builder slot feeds both funnels (businesses wanting AI + people wanting to build)

daily_item.slides: cover(story hook) + question-chain payload + pivot + cta (4-6 total, 7 only when the story truly demands it — the reference page tells bigger stories in 4; never pad)
daily_item.cover_rule: Single story: hook headline; if source video exists it is slide 2 as native video and cover swipe reads FULL VIDEO NEXT. One CTA only.
daily_item.payload_rule: QUESTION CHAIN: the cover plants a question; every next slide answers exactly that question (big statement headline + precise-details body) and plants the next one. Slide 2 doubles as SECOND COVER (IG re-serves skipped carousels with slide 2 as cover — must hook standalone). Bodies: SPOKEN VOICE (punch, plain-words explanation, kicker) with each slide adding ONE new fact in bold — never a stat wall, never finance-wire vocabulary. Then the VALUE slide ($100M Offers rules: owner's pain first, then the escape with a concrete number, minimal-effort framing, never price) — the consulting funnel lives here. THE FACTS STACK (owner Sep 4, @technology anatomy): exactly ONE inner slide is the stack — its body is the story's 3-4 hardest secondary facts, each on its OWN line (\n between lines), max 8 words per line, the number in each line accented. It reads in 3 seconds and is the slide people save; every other slide keeps the spoken-voice body.

builder_story.cadence: 2-3x weekly (takes a daily_item slot when a strong story exists)
builder_story.slides: cover + proof + how + engagement cta (4-5 total — measured from the @technology reference example; a tight 4-slide chain, never padded to 7)
builder_story.cover_rule: Hook = PERSON + outrageous concrete outcome with a number + effortless-or-forbidden twist ('A GUY MADE AN APP THAT TEXTED 800 GIRLS ON INSTAGRAM WHILE HE SLEPT'). Photo of the builder or product if available — here a face IS allowed because the story IS the person.
builder_story.payload_rule: Slide 2: PROOF — the product actually existing, doubles as SECOND COVER. Set product_shot: true on this slide when the story names the product's own website (the pipeline screenshots the real page); else the best article image. Headline answers the cover's 'wait, really?'. Slide 3: HOW — the AI stack/leverage + the numbers/timeline, in plain words a 16-year-old gets ('he typed what he wanted in plain English'). Each slide standalone mini-story, bold facts, rank/record framing.
builder_story.cta_rule: ENGAGEMENT CTA, not a follow pill — the reference example ends 'COMMENT "APP" AND WE'LL SEND YOU THE LINK'. Ours: invite the reader to comment/DM the exact word AI to get the tool/story link + what AI could do for their business. One concrete promise, no hype.
builder_story.audience: two funnels at once: businesses that want AI implemented, and people who want to build an AI business
builder_story.examples: Medvi (run by one person), solo founders at $1M+ ARR, tiny teams shipping what used to take 50 people

ai_education.slides: cover (N-promise hook) + 4-7 payload (one skill/story each) + cta (6-9 total)
ai_education.cover_rule: Cover promises a countable payoff with a number: 'N THINGS <TOOL> CAN DO...' or 'A GUY WHO CAN'T CODE BUILT...'. Scarcity subjects and everyday words only — 'a tool where you type plain English and it builds the whole app', never 'CLI' or 'agentic'.
ai_education.payload_rule: Two flavors, per @technology's measured how-to anatomy: (a) SKILL slide — 'N) IMPERATIVE VERB + the thing' headline, one caps sentence on WHY it matters, body = HOW TO in numbered steps 1-3 a total beginner can follow tonight; (b) BUILT-IT slide — a TRUE widely-reported story of a real person who built something (headline DNA: physical past-tense verb + number). NEVER invent people, numbers, or stories — if unsure it happened, use a capability demo instead. CTA = 'SAVE THIS' utility framing (saves are the ER engine for this container).
ai_education.audience: builders funnel + business owners seeing what's possible; the caption owner-CTA still closes with the DM 'AI' line
ai_education.topics: Claude Code powers, free AI powers anyone can use today, zero-coders who shipped real apps, one-sentence builds, AI doing a whole job overnight

media_rule.principle: The media is the visual argument for the headline — it must make the claim before the text is read. Select by the headline's emotional register, not its nouns.
media_rule.fallback: No image that passes -> big-type dark slide. A bad or generic image is worse than none.
media_rule.reject: stock-looking, watermarked, below 1000px wide, caption chips baked in, emotionally flat

caption_blocks.spec: Swipe instruction + one sentence naming the range of what's inside, exactly one emoji
Dense paragraph, every item named in sequence, comma separated, no line breaks
Zoom-out paragraph: what it means collectively

qa_gate: Cover SUMMARIZES the whole story in 12-25 words with its wildest true specifics — nothing withheld (owner flip Aug 1; edu N-promise covers stay short). Zero neutral news phrasing.
Cover promises a format (or a hook for daily_item), with exactly one CTA instruction
Accent (<em>) words read as the full claim standalone
Media matches the claim emotionally; no media that fails the reject list
Caption has all five blocks within ceilings
